fact: On 2 May 2025 the Congolese regulator ARPTC granted a telecommunications network and services licence to Starlink DRC SA, allowing it to operate as an internet service provider (Starlink).

Starlink's conventional satellite broadband service, needing a dedicated terminal, became available in the DRC after the May 2025 licence; no launch date given, so dated to the article's publication date.

ARPTC announced on Friday 2 May 2025 a network and telecommunications services licence for Starlink DRC S.A., a Congolese subsidiary of Starlink, confirming it may operate as an internet access provider; ARPTC said launch would follow within days.

ARPTC announced in a communique that Starlink DRC S.A. obtained a network and telecommunications services licence and is authorised to operate as an internet access provider in DRC, with launch planned within days (communique dated over the weekend of the 2 May 2025 article).

ARPTC's March 2024 communique stated Starlink had obtained no operating title and no equipment approval, and that use of the network or sale of its terminals was illegal; the May 2025 licence reversed this.

Radiocom Communications & Computers, an authorised Starlink reseller, sells Starlink equipment and Residential and Priority plans to customers in Kinshasa and elsewhere in DRC; its 16 July 2026 advisory says Kinshasa capacity on the Residential plan is exhausted for four to six months.
Somaf Group opened an office in Kindu, Maniema, on 2 April 2026 selling Starlink internet kits with unlimited connection to customers; it is also based in Lubumbashi and Kinshasa.

The article lists the Democratic Republic of the Congo among the 25 African countries where Starlink operates as of November 2025; it gives no COD-specific licence, seller or subscriber detail (published 2026-01, no other date).

fact: In March 2024 the regulator ARPTC banned the use of Starlink in COD over security concerns about armed groups.

MyBroadband's Starlink status table lists the Democratic Republic of Congo as 'Available' for Starlink (SpaceX), dated 17 July 2026; no provider or licence detail given.
Technomag lists DR Congo among 26 countries where Starlink is 'Active Now', as of the 29 June 2026 article date (no other date given).
The DRC banned Starlink in 2024 over fears rebel groups would use it; the article says the ban was reversed in 2025 (no dates given beyond the years).
Le360's May 2026 regulatory table lists RDC among the 29 African countries where Starlink has been granted a licence; no licence date given.
Semafor reports that Starlink has been blocked from approval in seven African countries including DR Congo, so it was not authorised there; no date for the block is given, article date used.

Government soldiers seized Starlink kits from four community radio outlets or consortia in Fizi Territory, South Kivu, on 8 July 2026 whenever users tried to activate them, and told journalists the kits would be returned only when the war ended; the seizure is tied to the security shutdown, not stated as unlicensed use, per CPJ.

On the instruction of the mayor of Baraka, Starlink kits of some humanitarian NGOs used as their connection were seized during the Baraka-Fizi telecoms cut; the document gives no seizure date, so the published date 2026-08-03 is used, per Congorassure.cd.
